metadata.description: A curated marketplace of tested Claude Code plugins by Omer Yehuda: Army (multi-agent orchestration), Toon Shorts (animated shorts), Code Court (decisions on trial), Customs (a first-filter scan of skills before you install), Bug ER (minimal-incision bug fixes), ATC (air traffic control for parallel sessions), Studio (AI film crew for explainer videos), The Critics' Table (3-star review), Skill Installer (install skills from GitHub), Mission Control (go or no-go before a release), The Academy (exams for skills), The Archive (one memory for every plugin), The Newsroom (release notes from commits) and Premiere (realistic short films).

plugins.name: army
plugins.description: A chief of staff that commands 18 specialist units (intel, engineering, defense, legal, comms, data, sales and more) as subagents, with 110+ on-demand specialist playbooks, cost-aware model routing, safety gates and local lessons-learned memory.

plugins.name: toon-shorts
plugins.description: Animated short creator: turns a true story into an original voiced, captioned 1080x1920 cartoon MP4 for Shorts/TikTok/Reels, with toon characters, parallax sets, karaoke captions (Hebrew RTL), and a self-reviewed preview.

plugins.name: court
plugins.description: Put any technical decision on trial. Opposing counsel argue each option from shared evidence, a judge who never saw your opinion rules, and the verdict names the conditions that would overturn it.

plugins.name: customs
plugins.description: Deprecated: Customs moved into skill-installer (/skill-installer:inspect), where it also gates every install. This stub only points you there and will be removed in the next release.

plugins.name: er
plugins.description: Your bug gets admitted, triaged, diagnosed and operated on with the smallest possible incision. A triage nurse, an attending, a surgeon and a discharge check, with a hard incision budget so a one-line bug never becomes a 40-file rewrite.

plugins.name: atc
plugins.description: Air traffic control for parallel Claude Code sessions: claim lanes, avoid collisions. Sessions claim lanes (file globs); a hook asks before one session edits a file in another's lane, and a clearance skill splits a big task across non-overlapping parallel pilots. Coordination, not a sandbox.

plugins.name: studio
plugins.description: A film crew of AI agents that turns a topic into a finished explainer video, vertical (1080x1920) or wide (1920x1080): writer, director, test-screening critic and editor produce a kinetic-typography MP4 with captions, optional free local AI narration and upload metadata. The trend desk films a trending tool from real screenshots and makes a wide video plus a Short. Local rendering with Pillow and ffmpeg.

plugins.name: critics
plugins.description: Three independent critics (presentation, kitchen, recipe) taste your work before it ships, then a head critic awards up to 3 stars with a short fix-before-serving list. Re-taste after fixes to see stars go up.

plugins.name: skill-installer
plugins.description: Install Claude skills from GitHub the safe way: a customs scan gates every install (CLEARED installs, SECONDARY INSPECTION asks, DENIED never installs), files come from one pinned commit, skills.lock.json records hashes, and audit rescans what you have. Includes the Customs inspector.

plugins.name: mission-control
plugins.description: Go or no-go before every release. A script collects the release facts (versions, changelogs, dirty tree), four stations report, and a flight director who never saw your opinion rules GO, HOLD or NO-GO. It never tags, pushes or deploys.

plugins.name: academy
plugins.description: No skill ships without passing the exam. An examiner writes missions from a skill's promise, the script runs each one with and without the skill in headless Claude Code, and the report card says GRADUATED, RETAKE or EXPELLED with pass rate, tokens, cost and time.

plugins.name: archive
plugins.description: One memory for every plugin. Searches the local records your other plugins already keep (court verdicts, bug charts, reviews, lessons, countdowns, exams) and answers with the file behind each claim. Read-only: it never moves or edits a record.

plugins.name: newsroom
plugins.description: Every release deserves a headline. A reporter reads the commits, an editor writes release notes, a changelog draft, social posts and video metadata, and a fact-checker cuts every claim that has no commit behind it. Drafts only: it never posts.

plugins.name: premiere
plugins.description: A film crew of AI agents for realistic short films. A director writes the shot list, a cinematographer writes one prompt per shot with a consistent look, you generate the stills with the image model you choose, a continuity check rejects bad frames, and ffmpeg cuts a graded, scored film with camera moves, in wide or vertical.
